text:
- chief complaint: difficulty swallowing solid foods (larger pieces) and chest pain on swallowing, for several weeks.
- history of present illness: the patient reports intermittent dysphagia to large food pieces with odchest pain on swallowing, worse with stress, a diet of pizza and burgers, increased alcohol and caffeine intake, and recent relocation. Barium swallow showed mild narrowing in the mid and lower esophagus. No weight loss; about 10 lb weight gain over the last month.
- physical examination: vitals stable (BP 133/70, afebrile, normal heart rate and respiratory rate, SpO2 100%). Oral exam unremarkable. No thyromegaly or adenopathy. Abdomen nondistended with active bowel sounds, mild epigastric tenderness that resolved on re-palpation, negative Murphy's sign, no peritoneal signs. Lungs clear bilaterally. Skin without rash, lesions, or bruising.
- symptoms experienced by the patient: dysphagia to solid foods, odynophagia (chest pain on swallowing), intermittent epigastric pain. No blood in stool or melena reported.
- new medications prescribed or changed: pantoprazole (Protonix) 40 mg once daily, taken first thing in the morning; sucralfate (Carafate) 1 g four times daily for one month.
- follow-up instructions: upper endoscopy scheduled in one week; change diet, reduce alcohol and caffeine, eat slowly and chew thoroughly, avoid citrus, fruits, and spicy foods until symptoms improve.
